items.text: The process that loads this table is not included in the available files. A thorough search turned up only one unrelated mention, a placeholder template built for a different table that happens to reference this table's staging area by default. It does not identify who actually writes to this table

Both this table and its staging area are confirmed active, refreshed as recently as today. A sample of the most recent data shows it comes from two distinct sources, a warehouse shipments feed and a process labeled 'Shipper Content Pass'. This is a gap in the available files, not evidence the loading process does not exist: the same situation was found on the customer segment table, but that table had been inactive for seven years, while this one is actively live

This is directly relevant to an open question on the warehouse supplier list: that table's safety-net process shows a few unresolved records pointing back to this table's staging area, implying something overrides its default settings to read from here. This table's staging area being confirmed active supports that such a process genuinely exists in production, but its code is absent from the available files, just like this table's own loader, so it remains unidentified

Unlike every other reference table reviewed so far in this project, this table's automatic key-numbering feature is turned off. Whatever process writes to this table must supply its own record key directly, rather than relying on the database to assign one

In a sample of the most recent data (79,644 rows), no invalid supplier, location, item or department codes were found. This is not a guarantee across the full table, which holds 755.7 million rows; a complete scan was not run

items.text: The process that loads new data into this table has not been located anywhere in the available files, even though the table and its staging area are both confirmed active and refreshed as recently as today
items.note: This is a large, actively growing table (755.7 million rows) central to warehouse shipment reporting, so confirming who loads it matters directly for migration planning, and would also resolve a related open question on the warehouse supplier list

blocks.text: A few things below are still not fully confirmed. We are sharing this table's analysis now rather than holding it back, because the rest of it is solid and these gaps are clearly called out here, not hidden.

items.text: Still unknown: who gets notified if this process fails.
items.note: We could not find the program that loads this table anywhere in the files we have, so we have no way to see who is notified if it fails.

items.text: Still unknown: whether this process runs on a set schedule.
items.note: Same root cause as alerts: without the loading program itself, we have no way to confirm how often it runs.
